about: The free quota of each AI provider of AUTOMAT, as data (docs/MAINTENANCE.md, "The budget of the free quotas"). tools/ai-quota.py reads it; change a number here, never in code. Every number has its source. "verified": false means the number could not be checked against the provider's documentation on the day it was written: it is a conservative value (lower than what the provider is believed to allow), and the live rate-limit headers and 429 answers of each call correct the budget at run time. A person who checks a number against the provider's page sets it, with the date, and "verified": true.

reserve.source: tools/ai-review.py asks two independent providers (three for a tier-B change) once each; one review is the diff, the failure and the checklist (MAX_DIFF, FAILURE_SHOWN, ANSWER_TOKENS), estimated here at 9,000 tokens

share_source: the owner's request of 2026-11-22: one candidate cannot drain a provider; at most half of a provider's daily budget goes to one candidate's fixes

priority.about: The owner's decision of 2026-11-24: the free AIs are used every day, always when needed, above all for real updates; what is left goes to self-evolution, drills and the like. tools/ai-quota.py priority_of() puts every piece of AI work in one of four classes by its branch: 1 security fixes, 2 updates of what ships to users (everything not named below: the engine and ad-blocking crates, Dark Reader, uBlock Origin's scriptlets, the filter lists, Python and Qt, the Breeze icons, the daily candidate, a fix of main), 3 updates of the CI and the tools, 4 background work (the AUTOMAT drill, the replay bench, self-evolution). A share of each provider's day is kept for classes 1 and 2 (reserve_share); classes 3 and 4 use only what is above it, and class 4 also pauses while work of class 1 or 2 is pending or retrying (AUTOMAT's memory holds its row of failures, of the last pending_days days). In the last release_hours hours before a provider's own reset, what is left above release_margin of its day goes to classes 3 and 4 too, so nothing is wasted.
priority.source: the owner's words of 2026-11-24 ("use the free AIs every day, always when needed, above all for real updates; what is left goes to self-evolution, drills etc."); 60 %, 3 hours, 10 % and 2 days are this repository's starting values, not the providers'

routing.source: a starting order only (strong: the agent that reads files and the largest context first; fast: the quickest answers first), unverified; tools/automat-route.py replaces it with the success rate AUTOMAT's memory records per provider and kind of task once a pair has min_samples attempts

Antigravity.what: Gemini's free tier, used by the Antigravity agent (one session reads and edits files in several requests) and by the reviewers through the Gemini API
Antigravity.source: requests_per_day and session_requests: this repository's own note of 2026-11-19 (.github/autofix/prompt.md: "about 20 model requests a day", "at most 10 steps"). The others: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits could not be reached on 2026-11-23; conservative values

reset.source: the Gemini API's quotas per day reset at midnight Pacific time, as remembered from ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits; the page could not be reached on 2026-11-24

Groq.source: tokens_per_minute: below this repository's own note (tools/ai-providers.py: "about 8,000 tokens a minute"). The others: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits could not be reached on 2026-11-23; conservative values

reset.source: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits could not be reached on 2026-11-24; Groq's own headers give the time to its next reset (x-ratelimit-reset-requests), which counts more; until a person checks it, the repository's own day (UTC)

OpenRouter.source: openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits could not be reached on 2026-11-23; conservative values (the lower daily limit of an account without purchased credits, as remembered, not checked)

account.source: every :free model of OpenRouter counts against ONE daily cap of the account, not one per model: 50 requests a day for an account that never bought credits, as remembered from openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits (not reachable on 2026-11-24). tools/ai-quota.py reads GET /api/v1/key with the key at the start of each run that holds it: a request cap of the day in its answer is taken (never above max_requests_per_day), is_free_tier true confirms the free-tier value; the count of the day comes from OpenRouter's own headers and its 429 "free-models-per-day"
